commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to select a patient by index
commitResults.messageBody:
Caregivers need a way to pick one patient and see their full record,
but there is no command to select a patient from the list.

Let's add `view INDEX`, which follows the same index rules and
invalid-index message as `delete` so the two commands behave
consistently. For now it only reports which patient was selected;
showing the details comes in later changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match view success message to the UI mockup
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command reports "Showing details of [NAME]", but the UI
mockup in the user guide shows "Showing patient: [NAME]".

Let's use the mockup's wording so the app matches its screenshot,
and add a test that checks the exact message text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track the viewed patient in the model
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel needs to know which patient to show, and must stay
correct when that patient is edited or deleted by another command.

Let's store the viewed patient in the Model as an observable value
that the view command sets and the UI can listen to.

ModelManager updates it when the address book changes:
* setPatient swaps in the new copy, e.g. after care info is added
* deletePatient clears it when the viewed patient is deleted
* setAddressBook clears it when the patient is no longer present,
  e.g. after clear

commitResults.messageTitle: List every command in the help window
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window only links to the AB3 user guide, which does not
describe MediConnect's commands.

Let's show every available command instead, with its format and a
one-line description. The add line uses the MVP format without tags,
and each format matches the user guide.

The list is kept in HelpCommand so a test can check that no command
is missing from it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add patient detail panel for the view command
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command selects a patient, but the patient list card shows
only a few fields, so caregivers still cannot see the full record.

Let's add a PatientDetailPanel beside the patient list. It shows all
of the viewed patient's fields and care lists, with "None recorded"
for an empty list and a placeholder before the first view.

The panel listens to the viewed patient in the model, so it updates
on its own when that patient is edited, deleted or cleared.

Also document the view command in the UG and DG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add NRIC and DOB field validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Patient stores NRIC and DOB as plain strings, so add accepts any
value for them, such as "S123" or "2021-02-30".

The MVP spec requires NRIC to follow the NRIC/FIN format and DOB to
be a valid date that is not in the future, to catch entry errors that
could lead to identifying the wrong patient.

Let's,
* add Nric and Dob field classes, following the existing Phone class
* store NRIC in uppercase so duplicate checks need no case handling
* store DOB as a LocalDate, which already rejects impossible dates
* parse both in add, and validate both when loading saved data
* document both formats in the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Update name, phone and address validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Name, Phone and Address use the AB3 rules and messages. Names allow
digits, phones only need 3 digits, and the messages differ from the
spec.

The MVP spec restricts names to letters, spaces, "/" and ".", and
phones to 8 digits with an optional +65, to catch entry errors early.

Let's,
* update the Name and Phone rules and all three messages to the spec
* reduce multiple spaces between words in names to one
* store phones without +65 so the same number is always shown the same
* update test fixtures with phones that are not 8 digits
* document the name and phone formats in the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Update storage and sample data for patients
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage error messages still refer to persons. The sample data is the
AB3 list of 6 people with the same date of birth and no care info, and
no test reads care lists from a data file.

New users should see a realistic record on first launch, and care
lists must survive being saved and loaded.

Let's,
* replace the person wording in storage error messages
* reduce the sample data to 4 patients, two with care info
* test that invalid NRIC and DOB values in a data file are rejected
* add care lists to a typical patient in the JSON test file

No test builds the sample data, which is only created when the app
starts without a data file. An invalid sample patient would crash the
app on first launch without any test failing.

Let's add a test that builds the sample address book and checks that
every sample patient is in it.
